pages.text: Ectenaspis is an asaphid trilobite from the Ordovician of the United States. Like most other trilobites, it would have been a seafloor dwelling animal, where it would have likely scavenged for food. Similar to its more famous relative Asaphus, Ectenaspis is known to have possessed eyestalks, giving this animal a great field of view. In contrast, however, Ectenaspis sports mirrored

spines protruding backwards from either side of its head segment. In addition to the spikes, it also possessed a horn-like projection at its front, perhaps aiding in shoveling the seafloor or in intraspecific competition.
